newsitem.title: USA: Former NY Yankee pleads guilty in gun case.
newsitem.headline: Former NY Yankee pleads guilty in gun case.

text.p: Former New York Yankees pitcher Steve Howe, whose baseball career was marred by his problems with drug abuse, pleaded guilty Thursday to carrying a loaded gun on board an airplane.
Howe, who pleaded guilty to a misdemeanor weapons charge in State Supreme Court in Queens, was sentenced to three years probation and 150 hours of community service.

The incident occurred June 24, just two days after the Yankees dropped Howe from their roster midseason. Howe checked a black bag with a loaded pistol at the Delta Airlines terminal at Kennedy International Airport, authorities said.
Howe, 38, was about to board a Delta flight to Montana, where he lives in Whitefish, they said.
Throughout his career, Howe, who was named National League Rookie of the Year in 1980, was troubled by drug problems.

He was suspended from professional baseball seven times for problems related to drug abuse. Along with pitching for the Yankees, he played with the Los Angeles Dodgers, the Minnesota Twins and the Texas Rangers.

His community service, to be served under the auspices of a local church in the New York City borough of Queens, will include working with youth with alcohol and drug abuse problems, authorities said.

"Mr. Howe, who, according to his attorneys, has fought substance abuse and addiction for many years, will be involved in reaching out to local people battling these same problems," said Queens District Attorney Richard Brown.
